section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1986
title: 20 Means Adopted. For Committing Suicides: A study of Suicide cases according to ‘Means Adopted’ for committing suicides revealed that the majority of persons committed suicides by ‘Poison’ during 1986 and 30.4% of the total suicides were accounted by this method. The second important means used for committing suicides was by ‘Hanging’ which accounted for 24.1% of the total suicides during 1986. It was followed by (percentage shown in brackets) ‘Drowning’ (13.1), ‘By Fire’ (10.1), ‘By Railways’ (5.5), ‘By Jumping’ (1.5), ‘By Fire-Arms’ (0.8), ‘By Weapons’ (0.6), ‘By Touching Electric Wires’ (0.5), ‘By Taking Sleeping Pills’ (0.5) and ‘By Machines’ (0.2). 12.7% of the total suicides registered during 1986 was shared by the suicides under unimportant causes grouped under ‘Other Causes’.
